short: Recording income and expenses when they occur, not when paid.
seoTitle: Accrual Accounting — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: Accrual accounting records income when it is earned and expenses when they are incurred, regardless of when money changes hands.
definition: Accrual accounting records income when it is earned and expenses when they are incurred, regardless of when money changes hands. A December sale paid in February is December's income.
bodyHtml:
Why Accrual Accounting matters

Accrual gives a truthful picture of a period's performance. Cash-basis records make a month look brilliant simply because an old invoice was finally paid.

How Accrual Accounting works in practice

It requires adjusting entries at period end for accrued expenses, prepayments and income earned but not billed. That work is exactly what makes month-on-month comparison meaningful.

faq.question: Which basis should a small business use?
faq.answer: Accrual for management reporting once there is credit involved; the statutory position depends on entity type and turnover.

faq.question: What is the main downside of accrual?
faq.answer: It shows profit that has not been collected, so it must always be read alongside cash flow.
